title: Radio Trio / Радио-трио

listeningReference.title: Soda Pop / KPop Demon Hunters
listeningReference.use: Rhythmic energy, call-and-response and arrangement only; original melody and owned invented lyrics.

prompt:
Create a COMPLETE ORIGINAL ninety-second bubblegum K-pop dance song for a cheerful family rhythm game. Title: "Radio Trio / Lumi-Tiko-Nori". This must be distinctly punchier, bouncier and more percussive than a gentle melodic dance-pop song. Brand-new melody, bassline, arrangement and hook. No borrowed tune or lyrics, no imitation of an existing recording.

TARGET144BPM, solid4/4. A strongly audible tight kick on EVERY beat, sharply defined handclap/snare on2and4, nimble syncopated elastic bass, crisp eighth-note closed hats, playful bright brass/synth stabs and short fizzy pluck answers. Clear strong downbeats and obvious upbeat accents; keep the drums loud and dry enough for a player to hear exactly when to land on musical platforms. Short drum fills mark phrase endings. Groove must feel immediate, confident, danceable and fun from the first two seconds. No fifteen-second intro. Maximum four-second pickup; first vocal hook before6seconds. No ambient washes, slow ballad section or long fade-out.

A playful human vocal trio trades short melodic phrases and answers, then joins for a very catchy repeated chorus. Lead tone bright, warm and appealing to children AND teenagers, lively precise consonants, not shrill or babyish. Contrasting answering voices can suggest three friendly characters. Sing invented melodic syllables ONLY; no ordinary meaningful words, narration or animal calls. Pronunciations: lumi-lai=LOO-mee-lie; tiko-ta=TEE-koh-tah; nori-no=NOH-ree-noh; tiri-tai=TEE-ree-tie; lari-rai=LAH-ree-rye. Make the vowel endings beautifully rhyme, short phrases with audible breathing gaps. Give each main syllable its own clear rhythmic note, principally eighths and quarters; avoid a continuous rapid rap. Occasionally sustain a final '-lai' or '-tai' for one or two beats over the continuing kick.

MAIN CHORUS (four matching call-and-response lines, strong identical rhythmic motif but original melody):
Lumi-lai, tiko-tai — tiri-tai!
Nori-no, nori-nai — lari-rai!
Tiko-ta, lumi-lai — tara-tai!
Lumi-tiko, nori-nai — tiri-tai!

VERSE COUPLETS:
Lumi-li, lumi-la — tiko-ti, tiko-ta!
Tiri-ri, tara-ra — lumi-li, lumi-la!
Nori-ni, nori-no — lari-li, lari-lo!
Tiko-ti, nori-no — lari-li, lari-lo!

BRIEF BREAK TAGS:
Tiko-ta! Nori-no! Lumi-lai! Tiri-tai!

Compact complete structure around90seconds: immediate percussive pickup -> opening hook -> bouncy verse -> big chorus -> very short rhythmic break with tags -> varied second verse -> final doubled chorus -> clean upbeat resolved ending. Maintain the SAME steady audible dance pulse through transitions, with brief musical rests for contrast, not silence or half-time slowdown. Prioritize an infectious sung hook and clearly articulated beat over lush sustained background texture. A full finished standalone song, not a demo or a short loop.
